research: docs/research/2026-11-winners-30d.md: the account's biggest ad of the last 30 days, ACH-SVIT-190-H3 ($19.9k, ROAS 2.36), is a 27 s closer: a warning line, why now, 'here's the secret' (how to get the offer), the free wallet, why it ends, 'don't wait'; real footage of the bag, no features. 113-H2 (16 s, ROAS 2.55) is the same idea in one shot. All ten openings of 190 and 198 are warnings.
What these three keep: the length (25-35 s), the warning openings, the offer from the first line, 'here's the secret', a picture of the real bag on every line, a voice talking to 'you'.

What they improve, each a different lever: P01 removes the last doubt at checkout (no code: the half price is already on the page, the wallet comes with the bag) and adds one proof shot (the hidden back pocket, the bag's anti-theft reason to buy); P02 anchors the price ($109.90 -> $54.95) and stacks what you get (two straps, the pocket, the leather, the wallet, free shipping, the 1-year warranty: order value is the ROAS lever); P03 adds a second real deadline for gift buyers (order by 14 December for the best chance before Christmas; 92% of Cyber Weekend buyers bought a gift, docs/research/2026-11-all-time-best-ad.md).

What they never copy: 190's 'today is the absolute last day' (said daily for weeks: the sale ends on 30 November, PLAYBOOK 2026-10-27) and 'Susan's closing sale' (invented): the deadline here is the real one, and no returns promise (Black Friday orders are final sale).
